title: Florida Senate, District 26
what_it_does: Represents District 26 in the Florida Senate; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: OPEN SEAT: Lori Berman (D) is term-limited (Ballotpedia). Ballotpedia snippets list Rep. David Silvers (D) in the Democratic primary and Rep. Rick Roth (R) in the Republican primary for SD 26; Yvette Drucker withdrew to run for Clerk (https://ballotpedia.org/Florida_State_Senate_District_26; https://floridapolitics.com/archives/760783-david-silvers-raises-56k-in-first-full-quarter-running-for-sd-26-quintupling-rick-roths-haul/). Primary results (and whether either faced a primary) could NOT be verified from snippets. Research limitation (Sept 2026): Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, dos.fl.gov, floridaelectionwatch.gov, Florida Politics and all news sites were blocked for fetching in this sandbox and the WebSearch budget was capped, so the roster is built only from search-result snippets; write-in/NPA qualifiers could not be checked. Positions are null because no snippet contained an explicit issue statement.

candidates.name: David Silvers
candidates.background: Silvers, a Democratic state representative from Palm Beach County, launched a 2026 campaign to succeed term-limited Sen. Lori Berman in SD 26 and led the field in early fundraising.
candidates.primary_result: Listed in Aug. 18, 2026 Democratic primary (Ballotpedia); result NOT verified.

record.item: Voted against SB 300 (2023), the 2023 law limiting most abortions to six weeks of pregnancy.
Voted against HB 1 (2023), the 2023 law that made every Florida student eligible for a state-funded scholarship usable at private schools or for home education.
Voted against SB 254 (2023), the 2023 law barring gender-affirming medical treatment for minors and restricting it for adults.
Voted against SB 7050 (2023), the 2023 elections law that raised penalties and shortened deadlines for third-party voter-registration groups and changed vote-by-mail and voter-roll procedures.

Voted against SB 2-A (Dec. 2022), the December 2022 property-insurance law that ended one-way attorney fees and assignment of benefits and created a state reinsurance program, a market-based approach; a vote for it is coded as leaning against more direct state intervention.
Voted against HB 1 (2021), the 2021 Combating Public Disorder law that created new riot-related offenses and penalties and let the state override local cuts to police budgets.
Voted against HB 5 (2022), the 2022 law limiting most abortions to 15 weeks.
Voted against HB 1557 (2022), the 2022 Parental Rights in Education law restricting classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity.
Voted against SB 90 (2021), the 2021 elections law that added identification requirements for mail-ballot requests and limited drop-box hours.

Voted against CS/CS/HB 1645 (2024), the 2024 energy law that removed climate change as a priority of state energy policy, repealed several renewable-energy goals and grant programs, banned offshore wind turbines in state waters and eased regulation of natural-gas pipelines; a vote for it is coded as leaning against promoting renewable energy.
